result.rationale: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema in addGuests.schema.ts is `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness refinement, and the handler's `uniqueGuests` filter only excludes emails already in booking.attendees (`!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`), so duplicate emails within a single request pass validation and are inserted via `createMany`. The client-side refine exists only in AddGuestsDialog.tsx, which any authed caller bypasses. The mechanism is verifiable line-by-line in the diff.

judged_text: The server schema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client dialog enforces, and the handler's uniqueGuests filter (addGuests.handler.ts lines 74-78) only removes emails already on the booking, so duplicate emails within one request pass validation and reach prisma createMany (lines 100-106). A direct tRPC mutation with guests ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] — the endpoint is authedProcedure, reachable by any logged-in user without the dialog — inserts two identical BookingAttendee rows: the attendee appears twice in the ICS attachment and receives duplicate copies of every guest email, permanently corrupting the booking's attendee list.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.schema.ts`, the server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is only `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not include any uniqueness refinement. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but it does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. Therefore a request like `['a@x.com','a@x.com']` (both not already attendees) will produce `uniqueGuests` containing both entries and will be passed to `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}})`, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows or at least attempting to, depending on DB constraints (not shown in the diff).
